gist: A run of numbered appendix notes (91)-(109) on the inward work: the will as the fire and basis of microcosmic recreation, drawn upward by love and fermented through the individual Logos, guarded against self-centers, inner idolatry, the phantastic region and over-haste, until Light penetrates the body and the residuum of the sensual medium gives body to the regenerate soul.

notes.point: Endorsing Kirchberger, Atwood says the fire through which the voice conducts Light is our chaotic will in potentiality, basis of microcosmic recreation. Only Arndt among Mystics grasps the Psalms.
The Key to the Work (Key of the House of David) comes from the desire of the lower, generative, fallen life opening into the heart life by exstasis.

What is above (feminine principle, Wisdom, heart life) suddenly draws the self-willed source up by love, making it passive; the paternal seed is drawn up. The feminine spirit caused the Fall and, advanced, the restoration, which exceeds what was lost.
St Martin's 'true pronunciation of the two great names' means the revealed utterance of God's life in man, ground of both Testaments. Polytheism deviates from the central principle.

Where the Word comes there is power and the danger of self-centers, key to the Second Commandment. A graven image is an utterance carved into the understanding spirit, worshipped inwardly; material idolatry is its weaker, lesser copy.

Initiates moved one another by words of power; Masons lost the magic Key. Words and true tools are found within, given as wanted; outward tools represent those in the Recess of Light. Religious systems persist by faith in the invisible.
Perfection: one's fundamental faith, the individual Logos, fermented to transmute body, soul and spirit; not meant to complete till the time comes.
Alchemical seeking tempts one to force the work; Norton and Ripley (red poppies: work burnt, restarted) warn against the self-willed magnet's haste.
The Crown is the Logos. God's purpose: through man's consent and operation, Lucifer's fallen body of the will becomes body to the Divine.
Engelbrecht lacked Behmen's penetration. The analogical sphere (Regio phantastica, Evester) has relative truth; Hermetists took only its essence's derived light; self-desire adulterates.
Regenerate bodies become like iron in the forge, invisible through inner Light; light thrown inward awakens its center to coruscate. Archetypal Light burns up all images; it is Truth.

Numbers order the Divine Law's creative development, known in theurgic art where spirit multiplies spirit into points, planes, cubes, materiality; so the Tetractys, basis of the philosophic stone, known in Regeneration.

Senses turn against the sensuous medium in the blood; hyperphysical exudation and tears replace natural secretion; the connate spirit, bereft of its understanding spirit, rallies from a new center. Will is noun, love adjective, their union 'I am'.
The sensual medium's residuum embodies the regenerate soul after its Cross; this earth becomes the Cross's punctum saliens. Haste to be good is self-will, empowering the contrary principle.

method.veiled: the fire here is our chaotic will in potentiality
method.plain: The 'fire' through which the Light is conducted is the person's own will in its unformed, potential state; it is the ground of inner ('microcosmic') re-creation.
method.basis: APP ¶97: Atwood glosses Kirchberger's 'fire' directly and calls it the basis of recreation.

also.text: it is the basis of our microcosmic recreation

method.veiled: the Divine Will makes use of the human voice as an organ for conducting the Light, through the fire
method.plain: The Divine Will is the agent; the human voice is its organ for conducting Light through the will (the fire).
method.basis: APP ¶97: Kirchberger's statement, which Atwood says is right; 'fire' glossed in the same note.
method.voice: QUOTED: Kirchberger (endorsed: 'It strikes me that he is right in this')

method.veiled: The Key to the Work, or into another life, the Key of the House of David
method.plain: Entry to the work is gained when the desire of the lower (generative, fallen) life opens upward into the heart life through exstasis.
method.basis: APP ¶97: 'is obtained from the desire of the lower life ... opening up into the heart life ... by exstasis'.

also.text: opening up into the heart life, or the medial life, or the celestial life, or the vegetable life, by exstasis

method.veiled: it is love which attracts
method.plain: What is above (feminine principle, Wisdom, heart life) draws the self-willed source upward like a magnet; the drawing power is love, and nothing else can move it from self-consciousness into self-oblivion.
method.basis: APP ¶98 states the mechanism directly.

also.text: forces, draws, attracts as by a magnet, the self-willed source upwards
Nothing else could move that principle from its self-conscious center into self-oblivion

method.veiled: The draw up is sudden and as at an instant; a sudden force of admiration does it
method.plain: The upward drawing happens suddenly, in an instant, set off by a surge of admiration.
method.basis: APP ¶98 literal statement.

method.veiled: this latter becomes transmuted into a passive feminine principle
method.plain: The self-willed source, drawn up, ceases to be self-assertive and becomes passive/receptive; what is drawn up is the seed or paternal principle of this life.
method.basis: APP ¶98: both sentences stated directly in the note.

also.text: The seed of this life, the paternal principle, is drawn up.

method.veiled: When the attraction is placed above instead of below a restoration of what was lost takes place and more also
method.plain: Redirecting desire from below to above reverses the Fall and yields more than was lost; the feminine spirit that caused the Fall causes the restoration in an advanced stage.
method.basis: APP ¶98.

also.text: As the feminine spirit is the cause of the Fall, so is it in an advanced stage, you know the cause of the restoration
for the second Adam is greater than the first

method.veiled: in the true pronunciation of the two great names
method.plain: Atwood reads St Martin's phrase as the revealed utterance of the life of God in man, the original ground of both Testaments.
method.basis: APP ¶98: 'namely, on the revealed utterance of the life of God in man'.
method.voice: QUOTED: St Martin (glossed and endorsed by Atwood)

method.veiled: the danger is the tendency in such gifted beings to set up self-centers
method.plain: When the Word gives power to an individual, the risk is that he makes himself a center apart from God; Atwood calls this the key to the Second Commandment as result of violating the First.
method.basis: APP ¶100: 'Where that Word comes there is power in an individual'; 'This is the key to the philosophy of the Second Commandment'.

also.text: Where that Word comes there is power in an individual

method.veiled: A graven image means a vocal utterance carved into the understanding spirit which conceives it by the desire of life
method.plain: The forbidden 'graven image' is an inner utterance fixed in the understanding and worshipped from the heart; this living inner idolatry is far more dangerous than material idols, its weakened, dead copies.
method.basis: APP ¶100 defines the term and compares the two kinds.

also.text: the image lives in the heart and the whole individual worships it
the danger and sin of the latter is as nothing compared to those of the former, for in it was vitality and efficacy

method.veiled: The Initiated moved one another on by words of power.
method.plain: Initiates advanced one another by effective words; these words (lost by the Masons with the 'magic Key') are found only by seeking within, in the subjective, fundamental life.
method.basis: APP ¶100: 'they want the words, which are only to be found by seeking them in the subjective, the fundamental life'.

also.text: which are only to be found by seeking them in the subjective, the fundamental life
the magic Key, which was so carefully prepared by the anonymous author of the Tractatus Aureus

method.veiled: The true tools also may be found on the way in
method.plain: The real instruments of the work are found on the inward way and given one by one as needed; outward tools only represent those in the Recess of Light and are consecrated only by purpose. This chunk does not explain the double Triangle or triple Tau.
method.basis: APP ¶100: 'they will be given one after another as they are wanted'; 'they are representatives of these that are in the Recess of Light'.

also.text: the double Triangle and triple Tau
they are representatives of these that are in the Recess of Light
they are meant for sacred use, and are so far consecrated on account of purpose

method.veiled: his fundamental faith, which is his individual Logos, perfectly elaborated --- i.e., fermented --- so as to transmute the whole being
method.plain: The work is to submit one's core faith (one's own Logos) to be fully worked through, 'fermented', until it transforms body, soul and spirit.
method.basis: APP ¶101 glosses 'elaborated' as 'fermented' and identifies faith with the individual Logos.

method.veiled: the birth of this life prevents the complete work
method.plain: Few perfect the work; it is not meant to be completed till 'the time comes'. What 'the birth of this life' refers to is not explained (see ambiguities).

also.text: it is not intended to be completed till the time comes

method.veiled: break the seals upon the book of life artificially in order to hasten the work
method.plain: Forcing the work faster than God's will allows is the chief danger of alchemical seeking; the self-willed magnet, acting before its time, works powerfully and destructively.
method.basis: APP ¶102: 'instead of waiting for God’s will and pleasure about it'; APP ¶103.

also.text: Haste is the Devil’s part
There is a swiftness in the self-willed magnet working powerfully and to destruction if suffered to do so before its time.

method.veiled: the similitude of red poppies
method.plain: Ripley's image for the failure caused by haste: the work is all burnt up and the artist must begin again.
method.basis: APP ¶103: 'the work gets all burnt up and the artist has to begin over again'.

method.veiled: The Crown, to use Behmen’s and de St Martin’s phrase, is the Logos.
method.plain: 'The Crown' means the Logos.
method.basis: APP ¶104 direct identity.

method.veiled: bring the self-willed opposition into subjection through man’s consent and operation
method.plain: The Divine aim: by human consent and work, the rebellious will is subdued so that the fallen body of the will becomes a ground and body for the Divine; this is the value of man.

also.text: the original fallen body of the will in Lucifer may become a ground and body to the Divine instead of being apostate
The body, the really efficient body of the Will, is at present alienated from and in rebellion

method.veiled: The wise called it the Regio phantastica
method.plain: The analogical/visionary sphere has only relative truth; true Hermetists used only the derived light of its essence, stripped of phantasmagoric form, and a deep intellect is drawn past it to the primary sources of life. Some may still see pretty truly if faithful of purpose without much self-desire (the passage is partly garbled; see ambiguities); self-desire adulterates.

also.text: it was as a pabalum for them, but only when deprived of all phantasmagoric form
A deep intellect will not stay in these spheres, it will be drawn deeper by gravitation to the primary sources of life
it is self-desire that adulterates
misconceive this Evester, as Paracelsus calls it

method.veiled: the body became as the iron in the forge, no longer visible as before, but penetrated through and swallowed up with the Light
method.plain: In regenerate men the body is penetrated by Light as iron in the forge; a body becomes invisible only through excess of light from within.

also.text: a body can only become invisible through excess of light from within it

method.veiled: that light thrown in to find its own center and origin which awakens that center at last and causes it to coruscate
method.plain: Light turned inward toward its own center and origin eventually awakens that center so that it shines out.
method.basis: APP ¶105: preceding clauses say we are visible because 'ours' is shut up in its center and that light emanates from the eye's focus; the antecedent is uncertain (see ambiguities).

method.veiled: When the archetypal Light is perceived, it burns up all anterior manifestation, images and representations
method.plain: Perceiving the archetypal Light consumes all prior images and representations; it is Truth, both objective and subjective, and transmutes into itself whatever is not combustible.

also.text: transmuting all that is not combustible into itself

method.veiled: through their personal representation in theurgic art, by which spirit is added to spirit and multiplied as offspring
method.plain: Numbers are the order of the Divine Law's creative development; their arithmetic is known through theurgic art, where spirit joins spirit and multiplies, producing points, planes, cubes that converge in materiality.
method.basis: APP ¶107: Atwood's 'notion of numbers considered theosophically'.

method.veiled: such an ens was the basis of the philosophic stone, a metaphysico-chemical birth
method.plain: The entity obtained by that spiritual multiplication (like Pythagorus's Tetractys) underlies the philosophic stone, a birth both metaphysical and chemical, produced under the creative law and verified in Regeneration.
method.basis: APP ¶108: 'The mystic Tetractys of Pythagorus was thus obtained'; 'this is known in Regeneration'.

also.text: proving itself doubly, triply, by a realization of the first represented will
this is known in Regeneration, individually proven and proving all

method.veiled: All the organs of the senses are brought to bear against the principle of sense or the sensuous medium in the blood
method.plain: The sense faculties are turned against the sensuous medium in the blood; the members that serve the natural work also serve the super-essential. This chunk does not explain 'the hands are taught to war'.

also.text: All members that work here for the natural work, work also for the super-essential.
the hands are taught to war and the fingers to fight

method.veiled: all natural secretion is superseded by super-essential hyperphysical exudation and tears
method.plain: A sign of the work: ordinary secretions give way to 'hyperphysical' exudation and tears. This chunk does not explain them further.

method.veiled: when the connate spirit is deprived of its understanding spirit
method.plain: A stage of loss: separated from its understanding spirit, the connate spirit's life drains away until, by self-realization, it rallies from a new center; imaged by the Iliad after Patroclus' death and Hercules' grief for Hylas.

also.text: life flows away, until by self-realization it rallies from a new center

method.veiled: will is the substantive or noun, love the qualitative adjective form; their union coming into self-expression is the verb affirmative, I am
method.plain: Grammar mirrors operations of the Spirit: will as noun, love as adjective, their union expressed as 'I am'.
method.basis: APP ¶109 direct statement.

method.veiled: The sensual medium must in the work be brought to its pivot, to its last ens.
method.plain: The sensual medium is reduced to its final essence; its residue supplies the body of the regenerate soul, after the soul has passed under its Cross. Earth is the crucible for souls as well as bodies.

also.text: The residuum from this medium supplies body to the regenerate soul
the earth is the crucible for souls as well as bodies

method.veiled: The power is integral if it be turned into earth
method.plain: Cited for the residuum ('earth') that embodies the regenerate soul: power is complete when it takes earthly body.
method.basis: APP ¶110: quoted right after the residuum supplying body and St Martin's earth-as-crucible.

method.veiled: this earth becomes the punctum saliens of the Divine Cross which before was its punctum
method.plain: The 'earth' (residuum of the sensual medium) changes from a mere point into the living, springing point of the Divine Cross. This chunk does not explain further.
method.basis: APP ¶110: 'this earth' follows the residuum/earth sentences; rendering of the Latin is ours (see translations, ambiguities).

method.veiled: it is the duty of man’s will to follow God’s Will as He, according to His time and measure, opens the way
method.plain: The operator must neither hurry nor overdo, even in striving to be good: haste to be perfect is self-will that defeats the end, and exceeding one's given capacity lets the contrary principle react. Religious self-will shows as spiritual pride, contempt, morbid self-anatomy, uncharity and odium theologicum.
method.basis: APP ¶110, including Solomon's saying and the Note.

also.text: Festina lente, Ne quid nimis
too much haste to be good or perfect involves a self-willed action which defeats the end
if we do, it gives power to the contrary principle to react upon the over-run
Be not righteous overmuch

ambiguities.quote: the heart life, or the medial life, or the celestial life, or the vegetable life
readings: Four names for one and the same higher life.
Alternative or successive levels into which the lower life may open.
ambiguities.basis: The 'or' series can be appositive or disjunctive; APP ¶98 names only 'the heart life' as that which is above, favouring synonymy without settling it.

ambiguities.quote: the celestial as well as the ultimate may be used
readings: Both celestial and outermost forms of the tools are permissible to use.
Both may be used freely because they lack the sacredness of the originals.
ambiguities.basis: APP ¶100: preceded by 'sacred in their originals; in their ultimates from the center they are not so'; followed by 'There is not that sacredness in the outward tools' yet 'they are meant for sacred use'.

ambiguities.quote: the birth of this life prevents the complete work
readings: The present natural life stands in the way of completion.
The birth of the new life itself marks a limit short of completion.
ambiguities.basis: APP ¶101: followed by 'it is not intended to be completed till the time comes', which fits either; 'this life' is unspecified.

ambiguities.quote: misconceive this Evester, as Paracelsus calls it, and having a see things pretty truly
readings: Text is corrupt; such visionaries, though misconceiving it, can still see fairly truly if faithful and free of self-desire.
'misconceive' may mean 'conceive in' (receive) the Evester rather than misunderstand it.
Words are missing after 'having a', so the conditions may be incomplete.
ambiguities.basis: The phrase 'having a see' is grammatically broken; the clause continues 'if they continue faithful of purpose without much self-desire; it is self-desire that adulterates'.

ambiguities.quote: Vaughan, the Welshman, very elegantly depicts the play of that ether.
readings: 'that ether' is the Regio phantastica / Evester just discussed.
'that ether' is some other medium not named in this chunk.
ambiguities.basis: The sentence follows directly on the Evester; no explicit identity is asserted.

ambiguities.quote: It is by shutting up of ours in its center that we become sensibly visible to sense
readings: 'ours' = our light, shut up in its center, so the body shows instead of shining.
'ours' = our eye or body, shut in its center.
ambiguities.basis: Preceded by 'a body can only become invisible through excess of light from within it' and the eye-and-iris image; the antecedent is unstated.

ambiguities.quote: this earth becomes the punctum saliens of the Divine Cross which before was its punctum
readings: The earth (residuum) changes from a fixed point into the living point of the Cross.
The Cross, formerly the earth's point, becomes its living point.
ambiguities.basis: The relative clause 'which before was its punctum' could refer to earth or to the Cross.

translations.translation: Make haste slowly; nothing in excess

threads.note: Notes are numbered (91)-(109); what they annotate is not stated in this chunk.
Points to the magic Key prepared by the anonymous author of the Tractatus Aureus (Museum Hermeticum, edit. 1649, p. 45).
